deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of §16 of Riemann's Inauguraldissertation (1851), the section that patches up the Dirichlet-principle argument. The quantity is L = ∫∫_T (λ_x² + λ_y²) dT. The claim being proved: λ cannot approach a function γ that has a jump along a line. More precisely, if λ is required to equal γ outside a strip T' around the jump line, then T' can be taken so thin that L > C for any given C.

The previous page sets up the notation:
- s is arc length along the discontinuity line and p is the signed normal distance.
- κ is the curvature, taken positive when the line is concave toward p > 0.
- p_1 > 0 and p_2 < 0 are the edges of T'.
- γ_1 and γ_2 are the values of γ there. Since λ = γ outside T', these are the boundary values λ_1 and λ_2.

(1) Contribution of a piece of the strip. Take a piece between the normals at two endpoints, assuming the strip does not reach the centres of curvature, so 1 − κp > 0. In the coordinates (s, p) the area element is (1 − κp) ds dp. The squared gradient is λ_p² + λ_s²/(1 − κp)². So the contribution to L is
∫ds ∫_{p2}^{p1} (1 − κp)[λ_p² + λ_s²/(1 − κp)²] dp.
Dropping the nonnegative λ_s term gives a lower bound by ∫ds ∫_{p2}^{p1} λ_p²(1 − κp) dp.

(2) One-dimensional minimisation ("nach bekannten Regeln"). Minimise J = ∫_{p2}^{p1} λ'(p)²(1 − κp) dp with λ(p_1) = λ_1 and λ(p_2) = λ_2. [Filled in by me:]
- The Euler–Lagrange equation is ((1 − κp)λ')' = 0, so (1 − κp)λ' = c.
- Hence λ = −(c/κ) log(1 − κp) + const.
- Write D = log(1 − κp_2) − log(1 − κp_1). Then λ_1 − λ_2 = cD/κ.
- J_min = c² ∫ dp/(1 − κp) = c² D/κ = (λ_1 − λ_2)² κ / D.
- Equivalently, by Cauchy–Schwarz, (λ_1 − λ_2)² ≤ J · ∫dp/(1 − κp).
This matches Riemann's formula. For κ → 0 it reduces to (λ_1 − λ_2)²/(p_1 − p_2).

(3) Consequence. Whatever λ is inside T', the contribution satisfies
contribution > ∫ (λ_1 − λ_2)² κ ds / [log(1 − κp_2) − log(1 − κp_1)].

(4) Making the bound large. Because γ jumps, λ_1 − λ_2 tends to a finite nonzero limit as p_1, p_2 → 0. So one can choose P_1 > 0 > P_2 such that (λ_1 − λ_2)² ≥ m > 0 for P_1 > p_1 > 0 and P_2 < p_2 < 0. Put
a = ∫ mκ ds / [log(1 − κP_2) − log(1 − κP_1)].
Require, pointwise in s, that log(1 − κp_1) > (a/C) log(1 − κP_1) and the corresponding inequality at p_2. [Filled in by me: written via D/κ = ∫dp/(1 − κp), this means D(p)/κ < (a/C)·D(P)/κ.] Then the integrand exceeds (C/a)·mκ/D(P), and the integral exceeds C. Solving for p gives Riemann's conditions:
- 0 < p_1 < (1 − (1 − κP_1)^{a/C})/κ, valid for either sign of κ;
- for p_2 (which is negative): (1 − (1 − κP_2)^{a/C})/κ < p_2 < 0.

(5) Footnote, first remark. One of P_1, P_2 may be taken = 0 if T' keeps finite width on one side. This covers a discontinuity along the boundary, or one created by altering γ along an interior line.

(6) Footnote, second remark. m need not be the minimum of (λ_1 − λ_2)². It suffices that, for every δ, values of p_1 and p_2 within δ exist with (λ_1 − λ_2)² > m. Such an m exists by the definition of a jump discontinuity. The bare-minimum version would fail if γ oscillated infinitely often near the line, e.g. γ ~ sin(1/p). In that case T' is chosen with its edges at such favourable p-values.
errors: The condition on p_2 is written '0 < p_2 < (1 − (1 − κP_2)^{a/C})/κ' (as far as the hand can be read). Since p_2 < 0, the correct statement is (1 − (1 − κP_2)^{a/C})/κ < p_2 < 0. This is a sign/orientation slip, or misreading, in the draft.
Implicit assumptions are not stated: a/C < 1 (C large), and 1 − κP_i > 0 so that the fractional powers make sense. The curvature-centre condition is stated; the others are not.

In the footnote's generalisation, the favourable p_1(s), p_2(s) must be chosen jointly over s (uniformity / measurability in s). This is passed over silently. It is harmless at Riemann's level of rigour but is an unproved step.

The overall Dirichlet-principle argument this lemma supports (existence of a minimiser of L) is the famously flawed step later criticised by Weierstrass. This page itself only proves a lower bound, which is fine.

results.what: Minimum of ∫_{p2}^{p1} λ'²(1 − κp) dp with fixed endpoint values equals (λ_1 − λ_2)²κ / [log(1 − κp_2) − log(1 − κp_1)] (Dirichlet energy across a curved strip in normal coordinates).
results.modern_name: 1D weighted Dirichlet problem / Euler–Lagrange or Cauchy–Schwarz lower bound; capacity of an annular strip
results.usually_credited_to: Standard calculus of variations; this specific use appears in Riemann's 1851 dissertation §16

results.what: Lemma: if the admissible function must equal a γ with a jump line outside a thin strip T', the Dirichlet integral can be made to exceed any C by thinning T'. So minimising sequences cannot converge to discontinuous γ.
results.modern_name: Lower bound on energy / capacity argument showing H^1 functions have no jump discontinuities (trace argument)

results.what: Footnote refinement replacing the minimum by a 'lim sup'-type threshold to handle oscillatory γ such as sin(1/p).
results.modern_name: Use of limsup/liminf of oscillation in place of a minimum

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of §16 of Riemann's published 1851 doctoral dissertation (the Dirichlet-principle repair lemma). The computation and the footnote appear essentially verbatim in the printed text, so nothing here is new or unattributed.

checkable.asserts: λ = −(c/κ)log(1 − κp) satisfies the Euler–Lagrange equation ((1 − κp)λ')' = 0 (result 0).
The minimum value ∫c²/(1 − κp)dp = c²D/κ equals (λ_1 − λ_2)²κ/D, with λ_1 − λ_2 = cD/κ (result 0).
∫_{p2}^{p1} dp/(1 − κp) = [log(1 − κp_2) − log(1 − κp_1)]/κ, assuming 1 − κp > 0 (result 0).
The flat limit gives 1/(p1 − p2), i.e. the straight-line minimum (λ_1 − λ_2)²/(p_1 − p_2).

transcription_corrections: Line 6: the hand reads 'sich aber noch [struck] bekannten Regeln' – likely 'nach' with a correction; the meaning is 'nach bekannten Regeln'.
The differences written as (λ_1 − λ_2) in the transcription look in the image like (γ_1 − γ_2), matching the previous page's notation. Mathematically identical, since λ = γ on the boundary of T'.
Condition on p_2: the image appears to read '0 < p_2 ≤ …', but the sense requires (1 − (1 − κP_2)^{a/C})/κ < p_2 < 0.
Footnote: 'wie klein man auch δ annehmen möge' – 'möge' appears struck/rewritten, and 'Werthe' is duplicated with one struck; the reading is otherwise fine.
Footnote last lines: '{+d+}' insertion before 'werden' ('unzulänglich würde/werden'), and 'γ unendlich viele Maxima und Minima' – the leading symbol is γ.
